newsitem.title: USA: Moore says to exit 2 government contracts.
newsitem.headline: Moore says to exit 2 government contracts.

text.p: Moore Medical Corp said Wednesday it has decided to exit its supply contracts with the U.S. Department of Veterans Affairs and the Defense Department, and will take a charge to historical earnings, expected to be between $2 million and $3.5 million, for certain price adjustments under the contracts.
The company said it will also take a $650,000 after-tax charge in 1997 for exiting the business.
The company said it is in contract discussions with the government and that the final charge will be subject to the outcome of those talks.
The company said that it is leaving the business due to its highly competitive nature, the complexity of contractual price compliance regulations and related administrative burdens.
From 1991 through 1996, sales to federal agencies aggregated approximately $50 million, or three percent of total company sales over those years.
